title: Retail Sales Performance 2023–2024: Verified Findings Report
executive_summary: Cleaned 2023–2024 data show total revenue of $445,325.09 across 520 orders. Revenue grew 10.08% year over year to $233,348.80 in 2024, with quarterly revenue peaking in Q3 ($71,674.99) before a Q4 dip. East leads regional revenue; order values are highly skewed (median $313.28 vs mean $856.39), while the top customer represents just 6.24% of revenue, so customer concentration risk is low.

key_findings.statement: Across the cleaned 2023–2024 data, total revenue was $445,325.09 on 520 orders, giving an average order value of $856.39.
East generated the most revenue ($130,516.69), ahead of North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16) and South ($90,534.49); East exceeded the lowest region, South, by $39,982.20.
2024 quarterly revenue rose from $36,108.31 in Q1 to $56,616.79 in Q2, peaked at $71,674.99 in Q3, then dipped to $68,948.71 in Q4; Q3 exceeded Q1 by $35,566.68.
Annual revenue increased from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, a year-over-year rise of 10.08% ($21,372.51).
22 Electronics orders carried discounts of at least 20%, totalling $50,035.33 — 11.24% of overall revenue from just 4.23% of all orders.
Order revenue is strongly right-skewed: mean $856.39 versus median $313.28 (mean 2.73x the median), standard deviation $1,295.74, with orders spanning $5.27 to $7,844.02.
There are 222 distinct customers; the largest accounts for $27,793.13, or 6.24% of total revenue, indicating low customer concentration.

limitations: The dataset spans only 2023–2024, so longer-term trends and repeatable seasonality cannot be established.
Only revenue is available; with no cost or margin fields, the profitability of the high-discount Electronics orders ($50,035.33) cannot be judged.
The average order value ($856.39) is inflated by a small number of very large orders (max $7,844.02) and is not typical (median $313.28).
Customer metrics assume customer_id values uniquely and consistently identify real customers.
The cause of the Q4 2024 dip ($68,948.71 vs $71,674.99 in Q3) cannot be determined from these data alone.
conclusion: 2024 closed with solid 10.08% growth and a strong Q3, but the Q4 slowdown, the lagging South region and heavy order-value skew warrant attention. Recommended next steps: investigate Q4 drivers, review deep-discount Electronics profitability, and track median—not just mean—order value.
